title: Why Japanese People NEVER Tip
description: A waiter literally chased a tourist down the street to return his tip. Here's why tipping in Japan is basically an insult.

sections.narration: A waiter in Tokyo just CHASED a tourist down the street. Waving money. Begging him to take it back.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: waiter in apron running on a city street, arm stretched out holding money bills, tourist boy turning around looking confused, Tokyo buildings in background

sections.narration: The tourist didn't steal anything. He left a TWENTY DOLLAR tip.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: close-up of money bills on a restaurant table next to empty sushi plates, a hand reaching for the money, question mark floating above
Centered: waiter standing with arms crossed looking serious, boy with sweat drops and wide eyes, large red X symbol between them

sections.narration: In Japan, tipping doesn't mean generous. It means you think they NEED charity.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy offering coins to waiter, waiter stepping back with both hands up in a stop gesture, speech bubble with sad face above waiter

sections.narration: Imagine handing your doctor five bucks and saying — wow, didn't think you'd actually do your job.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy holding out a small coin to a doctor in white coat, doctor staring at coin with a blank expression, giant question mark above doctor

sections.narration: That's EXACTLY how it feels. Because in Japan, perfection isn't a bonus. It's called omotenashi — and it's the MINIMUM.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: three panels showing Japanese workers - taxi driver bowing, store clerk wrapping a gift with ribbon, waiter pouring tea perfectly, glowing Japanese text omotenashi above

sections.narration: But here's what no one tells you. Japanese servers don't earn LESS without tips.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: Japanese waiter smiling and holding a full wallet, green upward arrow and checkmark beside him, restaurant background

sections.narration: They earn a LIVING WAGE. The price on the menu already covers fair pay.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: Japanese menu with price circled, equals sign pointing to happy waiter giving thumbs up, stack of coins and bills balanced on other side

sections.narration: Meanwhile in America? Servers make TWO dollars an hour. And HOPE you feel generous.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: American waiter looking down sadly holding two tiny coins, empty tip jar beside him, rain cloud floating above his head

sections.narration: So one country pays workers properly and gets world-class service. The other makes workers BEG.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: split screen with Japan flag and happy waiter on left side, American flag and sad waiter on right side, versus symbol in the middle

sections.narration: Japan figured this out CENTURIES ago. And that waiter who chased the tourist?
sections.visual_notes: Centered: ancient Japanese scroll with modern waiter figure, timeline showing centuries, lightbulb glowing above

sections.narration: He wasn't returning a tip. He was returning an INSULT.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: waiter politely handing money back to surprised tourist boy with a bow, sparkle effects around the waiter showing respect
